paper.title: Combinatorial Multi-armed Bandits: Arm Selection via Group Testing

settings.name_in_paper: CMAB with semi-bandit feedback and cardinality constraint (Bernoulli base arms, black-box reward)
unmapped: reward function r(S; mu) is unknown but accessible via black-box evaluation queries at any parameter theta
reward depends only on base-arm means (Assumption 1), is monotone in S (Assumption 3), bounded in [0,M] with M known (Assumption 4)
separable reward (Assumption 6): adding an optimal arm yields strictly higher reward than adding a sub-optimal arm
the learner knows the CDF of the minimum gap Delta_min(mu) (Assumption 5); the instance's minimum gap is treated as random
the learner knows the reward bound M
paper's m is the number of base arms; paper's K (canonical m) is the cardinality bound on super-arms
settings.definition_quote: we consider a CMAB setting with $m$ arms... Each arm $i\in[m]$ is associated with an independent Bernoulli distribution with an \emph{unknown} mean $\mu_i$... We consider the semi-bandit feedback model... Function $r$ is assumed to be \emph{unknown}, and the learner only has {\em black-box} access to it... we impose that the cardinality of the optimal super-arm $|\mcS| \leq K\in[m]$.

algorithms.name: GT+QTS (Group Testing + Quantized Thompson Sampling)
requires_knowledge_of: CDF of Delta_min (to set quantization level)

symbols.Dt_i: min over super-arms S containing base arm i of (Delta(S,mu) - Delta_min(mu)/2 - (K^2+2) B eps)
symbols.L_lip: Lipschitz constant B of the reward (l1 norm)

conditions: Assumptions 1-6: reward depends only on means, B-Lipschitz in l1, monotone, bounded in [0,M] with M known, CDF of Delta_min known, separable reward
holds with probability at least 1-2*gamma (over the random minimum gap)
tuning: quantization level Delta = F_mu^{-1}(gamma), gamma in [0,1/2]
number of tests per round per Lemma 1

source.label: theorem: regret upper bound
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{assumption: mean only}--\ref{assumption: C separability}, by setting $\delta = \frac{1}{t^2}$, and the quantization level $\Delta:= \mathbb{F}^{-1}_{\bmu}(\gamma)$ for any $\gamma\in[0,1/2]$, with probability at least $1-2\gamma$, the regret of the GT+QTS algorithm satisfies \mathfrak{R}(T) \leq \sum_{i\in[m]} (2\log K + 6)B^2 \times\frac{\log(2^m|\mcI|T)}{\min_{\mcS : i\in\mcS}(\Delta(\mcS,\bmu) - \frac{\Delta_{\min}(\bmu)}{2}-(K^2+2)B\varepsilon)} + (...)\Delta_{\max}(\bmu), where $\alpha\in\R_+$ is a constant, and $\varepsilon$ is chosen as $\varepsilon<\frac{\Delta_{\min}(\bmu)}{4B(K^2 + 2)}$.

results.notes: Regret defined as sum_t E[Delta(S(t),mu)] => pseudo-regret; the bound on this expectation holds with probability >=1-2gamma over the randomness of the instance's minimum gap, recorded as high_probability. Paper summarizes as O(m Delta_min^{-1} log K log T). Oracle uses O(log m) reward evaluations per round (Lemma 1), not recorded as a regret result.
